summary.tldr: Adds telecom security powers and creates rules to protect cyber systems used by federally regulated services tied to national security or public safety.
what_it_does: Adds security of the Canadian telecommunications system as a policy objective and lets the Governor in Council and the Minister of Industry order telecom providers to do, or stop doing, things needed to secure it.
Creates an administrative monetary penalty scheme for not following telecom security orders and regulations, and sets rules for judicial review of those decisions.
Enacts the Critical Cyber Systems Protection Act for services and systems important to national security or public safety and within federal authority.
Lets the Governor in Council designate a service or system and set classes of operators for it.
Requires designated operators to create cyber security programs, reduce supply-chain and third-party risks, report cyber security incidents, and follow cyber security directions.
Provides for information sharing and enforcement, including consequences for non-compliance.
who_it_affects: Operators of federally regulated cyber systems
summary.background: Bill C-26 was introduced in the House of Commons on 14 June 2022. It has two parts, one amending the Telecommunications Act and one enacting the Critical Cyber Systems Protection Act.
